subject: [PATCH 0/3] block: skip the blkcg walk in blk_cgroup_congested() when nothing is throttled

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author responded to a concern about blkcg_clear_delay() overwriting state managed by other policies, explaining that the issue is specific to cases where multiple block cgroup policies coexist on the same device and one policy's data is freed while the other remains active. The author suggests that this scenario might not be common enough to warrant addressing.
sentiment_signals: questioning the severity of the issue
expressing uncertainty about whether it needs to be addressed
reviews.raw_body:
Sashiko reported:

---
[Severity: High]
Does this unconditional call to blkcg_clear_delay() overwrite state managed
by other policies?

Since use_delay is shared among block cgroup policies, if iocost never
actually applied a delay, this might forcefully zero out the delay state
managed by other active policies like blk-iolatency. 

Would it be safer to check if iocost had actually set a delay before clearing
it here?
---


My understanding is that this requires both policies to coexist on the same
device/blkg?

I believe the main problematic sequence would be:

  1. io.latency owns positive use_delay.
  2. io.cost policy data exists but may never have delayed anything.
  3. io.cost policy data is freed while the blkg survives.
  4. Its unconditional clear removes io.latency\u2019s state.

With only one policy, the terminal clear is correct and clearing zero is harmless.

The concern is narrower still: ordinary disk/cgroup destruction removes the whole
blkg, so the main observable case is one-policy activation rollback or deactivation
while the other remains active.

I am not sure if this is something that is done by users? So might not need
to be addressed?

Thanks,
Usama

reviews.author: Tejun Heo
reviews.summary: Reviewer Tejun Heo asked when the blkg pointer could be NULL in blk_cgroup_congested(), indicating a potential issue that needs to be addressed.
reviews.raw_body:
When can blkg be NULL here?

Thanks.

-- 
tejun

reviews.author: Tejun Heo
reviews.summary: Reviewer Tejun Heo stated that the two mechanisms (blkcg walk in blk_cgroup_congested() and use_delay being cleared) are not usually used together, and when they do interfere, it's a transient issue that doesn't cause any problems.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah, this is fine. The two mechanisms aren't usually used together and even
when they step on each other, use_delay being cleared spuriously is
transient and nothing really breaks.

Thanks.

-- 
tejun

2026-08-10.patch_summary: This patch set optimizes the blk_cgroup_congested() function by skipping unnecessary walks of the block cgroup (blkcg) hierarchy when no tasks are being throttled. The current implementation incurs a significant performance cost due to frequent cache line loads and RCU read-side pairs, especially in systems with deep container hierarchies. To address this, the patch introduces a global gate that only performs the walk when there is at least one blkcg with a non-zero congestion count. Additionally, two patches fix issues that can leave a blkcg permanently marked congested, which would otherwise cause unnecessary throttling of tasks in affected cgroups.

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author responded to Tejun Heo's feedback that pd->blkg is only set when the pd is attached to a blkg, and explained that the pd never had ->blkg assigned in the GFP_NOWAIT allocation failure case, so it reads as NULL rather than garbage.
reviews.raw_body:
Not in the normal case.

pd->blkg is only set when the pd is attached to a blkg.
blkcg_activate_policy() pre-allocates one outside the queue_lock when the
GFP_NOWAIT allocation fails, and frees it through pd_free_fn() if it ends up
unused \u2014 both at the retry and at the out: label. That pd never had ->blkg assigned.
It reads as NULL rather than garbage because iolatency_pd_alloc() uses kzalloc_node().

Good to keep as a guard in this case?

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged the need for revisions to address Tejun Heo's feedback and agreed to restructure in a new version (v2) of the patch.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks! Ack on all 3. I will wait a day incase there are more comments
and send a new revision tomorrow with all 3 addressed.
